To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ex vivo expansion of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) in hypoxic culture environment and transient adaptation of ex vivo expanded cells to autologous serum prior to transplantation would enhance the efficacy of MSCs in cell based therapy.
hypoxia and autologous serum supplementation can be used as a pre-transplantation strategy to enhance the efficacy of MSCs.
transient expansion of MSCs under normoxic condition using autologous serum may enhance the therapeutic efficacy of MSCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of pre-transplantation conditions to enhance the efficacy of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) transplantation.
the development of a new strategy to improve the efficacy of MSCs in regenerative medicine.

development of a novel strategy for ex vivo expansion of autologous MSCs using well defined media and autologous serum for transient adaptation prior to transplantation for enhancing regenerative benefits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transient adaptation of ex vivo expanded cells in autologous medium would be beneficial to increase the efficacy of transplanted cells.
the pre-transplantation adaptation in autologus serum supplemented medium is essential to improve the efficacy of ex vivo expanded autologous MSCs.

transient adaptation of ex vivo expanded autologous MSCs in autogenous serum supplemented medium prior transplantation would be an effective and efficient strategy to enhance the efficacy of ex vivo expanded and autologous MSC transplantation for regenerative medicine applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ex vivo expansion of human bone marrow MSCs under hypoxic condition in serum free media is a promising approach to generate large numbers of MSCs with high proliferative and differentiation potential, which can be used in clinical settings.
the pre-transplantation conditioning of MSCs in autogenous serum would help to increase the efficacy of ex vivo expanded autologous MSCs in regenerative medicine.
transient adaptation of expanded cells in autologous conditioned media prior to transplantation would be a better approach to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of ex vivo expanded cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transient adaptation of ex vivo expanded cells in autologous sera supplemented medium prior to transplant would enhance their efficacy.
the transient adaptation of MSCs in autogous serum supplemented medium would help to enhance the regenerative efficacy of ex vivo expanded autologous MSCs.
transient adaptation of expanded human MSCs in autogous serum supplemented medium can be used to improve the efficacy of MSCs for regenerative therapy.
